Subject: Subprocessor confirmation for EU migration

Hi Kimberly,

We're preparing the final migration window for our EU tenant next month and need to confirm Redwood's processor roster and a couple of technical guarantees so our compliance team can sign off. Specifically, can you provide:  

- A current subprocessor roster (names, primary function, primary location of processing).
- Confirmation that all transit and in-rest encryption controls meet our policy (TLS 1.2+ for transit and AES-256 or equivalent for storage).
- Whether any subprocessor will transfer data outside the EU in the course of processing for GreenFin. If so, which ones and what legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, etc.) is used.
- A short attestation (PDF) we can include in our audit packet that states the above items and notes any exceptions for the migration.

Can you please reply by EOD Wednesday (2029-04-17)? We're on a tight timeline because the migration calendar is locked.

Thanks,
Oliver Quinn

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear checklist. I've attached our current subprocessor roster (redwood-subprocessor-roster-20290415.csv) and a one-page transit encryption attestation (transit-encryption-attestation-20290415.pdf). High-level answers below:  

• Subprocessor roster: see attached CSV. We include vendor name, primary function (e.g., observability, object storage, CDN), and the primary processing country in the file. The roster reflects the roster we maintain for DPAs and SOC audits as of 2029-04-15.

• Encryption in transit & at rest: Redwood enforces TLS 1.2+ for all external and internal RPCs; we have rolled TLS 1.3 across public endpoints. At rest, we use AES-256-GCM or equivalent for persistent storage of customer data. The attestation PDF references specific cipher baselines and key rotation cadence.

• Cross-border transfers: For the vendors listed that process or route traffic through non-EU regions, we rely on SCCs and documented transfer impact assessments. The roster marks processors that might transit traffic through non-EU peering points. For GreenFin specifically, we do not send customer content to US-based processors for model inference; inference occurs in EU-hosted pools you pinned during onboarding. Some peripheral services (metrics aggregation, analytics ingest) may use global endpoints; these are flagged in the roster with SCCs applied.

• Next steps / timeline: If you need a signed attestation on company letterhead, we can provide that within 48 hours. For a deeper security review (SOC2 artifacts, encryption key handling details), please open the HubSpot ticket (GF-0009342) and we'll schedule a short remediation call with Naomi.

I've included Naomi (security) and Marissa (privacy & contracts) on the thread to help with any redlines or legal questions.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick follow-up from Privacy/Contracts:

Thanks for the attachments, Kimberly — roster looks complete. Two asks from our side so GreenFin's procurement team has everything they need:  

1) Can you confirm the KMS provider(s) listed for keys that protect GreenFin tenant data? The roster shows "CloudKMS Ltd" but doesn't say whether keys are customer-managed (CMK) or Redwood-managed. For EU-regulated customers we often recommend CMKs.  

2) Please confirm whether any of the flagged processors perform persistent logging that contains tenant-level content (not just metadata). If so, which processors and what retention window?

If GreenFin needs to keep processing strictly within EU borders, we can prepare a narrow scope project to route all telemetry and analytics to EU-only endpoints and provide a scoped amendment to the DPA. Naomi — can you pick up the technical KMS/retention answers and we can draft the amendment language if needed?

—Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

1) Can you provide a one-paragraph confirmation that keys protecting customer content can be scoped to EU-only KMS endpoints (even if Redwood manages rotation), or alternatively confirm the timeline to make keys customer-managed?
